Thereafter the respondent No. 2 filed a case being No. 69(4)91 in the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Jamalpur under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for redemption of the Mortgaged land and restoration of possession. The petition is annexed-as Annexure-I. Petitioner against the said case filed written objection before the Upazila Magistrate denying all the allegations as false and an illegal claim. A true copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-J the learned Upazila Magistrate on misconception of law by 14.4 order dated 9.3.92 allowed the application and directing the petitioner to restore possession of the case land to the respondent No. 2 within 15 days. A true copy of the order is annexed an Annexure-K. 

 6. The relevant fact in Writ Petition No. 1751/92 is that the respondent No. 2 to purchase better land at a suitable place being the exclusive owner and possession of the case land measuring an area of .30 acres in C.S. Plot No. 20 corresponding to R.O.R. Plot No. 43 and 44 of C.S. Khatian No. 4 corresponding to R.O.R. Khatian No. 8 of Mouza Sonkada Upazila Sadar, Jamalpur District proposed to sell the same to the petitioner at the market price amounting to Tk. 18,000/-. The petitioner agreed to purchase the same and the respondent No. 2 on receipt of the price of Tk. 18,000/- executed a sale deed. The photo copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-A. In terms of the sale deed the vendor respondent No. 2 handed over the possession to the petitioner within the knowledge of all concerned and then the respondent requested the petitioner to execute a deed of agreement for re conveyance with a promise that he would recover the case land within 2 years 11 months and in case of failure to pay the consideration money the kabala would be treated as an out of out sale forfeiting the right of re conveyance. Photo copy of the same is annexed an Annexure-Al. The petitioner after purchase developed the land and mutated his name without any objection and opened a separate Khatian No. 222 at yearly rent of Tk 2.25 along with the purchased land of .30 decimals including other purchased land necessary .45 acres from the same vendor in Mutation Case No. 1495(IX-1). The mutation khs.1".....1 and the duplicate carbon receipt are annexed as Annexure B and C respectively. While the petitioner possessing the same respondent No, 2 filed a case in respect of 2 different purchase deeds being case No. 152/89-90 under section 11 of Bangladesh Rin Shalishi Act 1989 (Act 15 of 1989) before the Chairman Upazila Rin Shalishi Board alleging that he took loan from the petitioner amounting to Tk. 18,000/- and for another deed an amount of Tk. 50,000/- to be repaid to the petitioner by installments. On receipt of the notice the petitioner appeared and filed written objection denying all allegations contending that those were false, concocted and highly malafide and after hearing both the parties the Rin Shalishi Board dismissed the same on 30.7.90. Against which respondent No. 2 preferred an appeal being No. 21 (XIX) of 1990 to the Appellate Authority, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Jamalpur who after perusing the materials on record dis-missed the appeal upholding the order of the Rin Shalishi Board by his order dated 20.1.91. The petitioner order of the Board and the dismissal order are annexed as Annexure-D and E and F respectively. Thereafter respondent No. 2 filed a case being No. 70(4)91 in the court of the Upazila Magistrate under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act praying for redemption of the mortgaged land and restoration of possession of the same. The true copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-G. Petitioner filed written objection against the same before the Upazila Magistrate denying the allegations as an illegal claim. True copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-H. The learned Upazila Magistrate allowed the redemption case and directed the petitioner to handover possession within 15 days by his order dated 9.3.92. The certified copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-I. 

 8. Mr. M.A. Wahab Miah the learned Advocate appearing in both the petitions submits that the Upazila Magistrate acted illegally and without any lawful authority holding that the alleged deed being supported by a deed of re-convenience comes within the mischief of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act being an unsufructory mortgage and the respondents are entitled to get possession, in clear violation of law since the grievance of the respondent No. 2 had already been decided by the appropriate Rin Shalishi Board. He submits that the respondent no. 2 went to Rin Shalishi Board for re conveyance of his land and being unsuccessful he preferred appeal before the Additional District Magistrate, Jamalpur who also on hearing and on perusal of the record dismissed the appeals affirming the order of the Rin Shalishi Board and in view of the fact the order of the Additional District Magistrate is final as provided under section 19 of the Rin Shalishi Ain, the respondent No. 2 is barred to move any application under section 95 A of the S.A.T. Act for the selfsame relief an because it has been finally decided. Mr. Wahab lastly contends that by filing a written objection before the Upazila Magistrate the petitioner challenged the jurisdiction of the court regarding the application for redemption as Res judicata when a competent jurisdiction decided the matter finally. But the learned Upazila Magistrate did not at all consider this important aspect of the matter and the legal position. 

 (গ) “খায়খালাসী বন্দক” অর্থ State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (E.B. Act XXVIII of 1951) এর Section 2(6) এ সংজায়িত “complete usufructuary mortgage”; 

 11. It appears that in both the cases transaction did not exceed admittedly 30,000/- by each document, i.e. one document was for 30,000/- and another was for 18,000/- and the precondition to file cases before the Board is that when land was sold facing distress due to natural calamity or some other reasonable hard-ship of living. But it appears that no averment have been made, in the agreements or in the recital of both the kabalas, to that effect instead in the recital it have been stated that both the transactions were intended by the vendor to purchase better and a suitable land. It further appears that admittedly the cases were filed beyond the statutory period of 6 months from the date of constitution of the Board or sale. We find that Rin Shalishi Board rightly decided the cases of the respondent No. 2 touching all the points and dismissed those. 

 13. On such facts it appears that the respondent No. 2 unsuccessfully moved up to the appellate forum and then being failure took resort to move the Upazila Magistrate under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for redemption pleading the same grievance as were before the Rin Shalishi Board. There is no denial about the principles laid down by their Lordship in the decision referred by the learned Advocate for the respondent but it has got no manner of application in the 'facts and circumstances of the present cases which are quite distinguishable. Mr: Abu Taher Howlader the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2 failed to show us any law that the petitioner being failure in the final forum for the same self-grievance can avail the other forum as in the cases. Our answer is also in the negative. The cases of the Respondent No. 2 were dis-missed by the Rin Salishi Board, the competent authority to decide the alleged grievance and then he went to the Appellate authority, Additional District Magistrate under section 19 of the Ain (Act), and he being the final authority also dismissed the appeals. Respondent No. 2 cannot move again afresh for the same relief to the alternative forum since his grievances have already been decided finally by the Appellate authority. There must be end of litigation.
